items.evidence: After page.reload() the spec checks that the Name field has the value "E2E Zip Hoodie" and that the page-header title shows it. Both values are read back from the server, so they would fail if the save mutation never ran.

Criterion 1 is asserted after saving: the page-header title shows newName, plus toHaveTitle. Criterion 2 is asserted after the reload: toHaveValue on the Name field and the header title both show the new name.
No page object in e2e/pages covers products, and no existing helper or constant is copied. The spec reuses PRODUCTS and ORDERS_SCENARIO from scenarios/orders.ts.
There is no waitForTimeout or sleep. The expect().toPass() retry is Playwright's retrying assertion, not a loop with a fixed delay.
It imports test and expect from fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to .cache or the dumps.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:41 finds the product-name cell with the CSS selector 'td[role="gridcell"][id^="glide-cell-1-"]', which relies on Glide's generated cell ids and a column position. A role-based gridcell locator filtered by name could be used instead.
The spec creates no data. It opens the scenario's existing E2E Hoodie through the products list and performs only the action under test.
No ids are hard-coded; the product is reached through search. Values come from the orders scenario's PRODUCTS.hoodie, not from populatedb.
It uses the fixture's default admin session, with no UI login and no credentials in the spec.
The spec is under e2e/tests/products/, and typecheck.txt reports exit 0 with no errors.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:25 defines every locator (search input, grid canvas, row anchor, name input, save button, header, toast) and the multi-step hover-and-open-row flow inline in the spec, instead of on a new ProductPage page object.
The change adds no page-object members, so this item does not apply.
The spec has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments, which is the suite's pattern.
It is one test with a test.step for each stage: open, rename and save, reload and verify.
The title "Staff renames a product and the new name persists after reload #e2e" describes the behaviour and carries the #e2e tag.
A doc comment at the top of the file says it covers renaming a product from its page and checking that the name persists after a reload.
The UI assertions are web-first. The getAttribute and boundingBox reads are only used to work out where to move the mouse.
e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:38 types the product name into the URL regex /query=E2E(%20|\+)Hoodie/ instead of building it from PRODUCTS.hoodie.name.
There is no cleanup code and no unique or timestamped names.
e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:50 passes explicit { timeout: 1000 } to getAttribute, boundingBox and toHaveAttribute (also line 61), and no comment gives a reason.
The relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
There is no any, no cast and no gql call.
e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:72 has numbered comments that repeat the next line, such as "// 4. Fill the Name textbox with the new name" and "// 5. Click Save" (also lines 35 and 86).

structured_output.summary: The rename test does its job: after a reload it reads the name back from the server and checks both the field and the header, so both acceptance criteria are covered and would fail if the save broke. It type-checks with no errors, uses the orders scenario and the fixture, and leaves no data behind. One blocker fails: B6, because the name cell is found by its Glide-generated cell id and column position. Four minors fail: M1 (every locator is inline in the spec, with no ProductPage page object), M8 (the product name is typed into the URL regex instead of using PRODUCTS.hoodie.name), M10 (explicit 1000ms timeouts with no reason given) and M13 (numbered comments that repeat the next line).
